newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel frees women prisoners after court decision.
newsitem.headline: Israel frees women prisoners after court decision.

text.p: Israel resumed its release of 31 Palestinian prisoners on Tuesday after the High Court rejected a last-minute petition to keep nine of them behind bars, witnesses said.
The women boarded buses at the Sharon and Neve Tirza prisons in central Israel on their way to Ramallah in the West Bank where Palestinian President Yasser Arafat waited to greet them.

Police detained two right-wing activists protesting against the release outside the prison, witnesses said. The women, among them two convicted killers, all signed commitments to refrain from violence.

The "Families of Arab Terror" group had asked the court to halt the release of the nine, saying they were arrested after the Israeli-Palestine Liberation Organisation agreements and were not eligible for freedom. Israel committed to release women prisoners in its 1995 peace deal with PLO.
Three of the women slated for release had already been freed but the others refused to leave prison until authorities allowed all 31 to go free.
"During these moments the prisoner release has begun...after the High Court rejected the petition," said a police spokeswoman.

Lamya Maarouf, a 32-year-old Brazilian citizen, was the first women released from the prison in Tel Mond at around 4 p.m. (1400 GMT). Israeli and Palestinian officials said she would be deported to Brazil.
Maarouf was arrested in 1986 for driving the car in which Israeli soldier David Manos was kidnapped. Manos was killed and Maarouf was sentenced to 25 years in jail.
"We did not know that the rest were not released when we left," said Aisha Abu Hazem, 23, one of three women freed before the high court hearing.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, paying hospital visits in the north to soldiers wounded in Lebanon, said the promise to free the women had been made originally by the previous Labour government.
"It's not a tactic, we are serious about fulfilling commitments, but we intend fully to see that there is an equal reciprocity on the other side," Netanyahu told reporters.

Israel has demanded the PLO keep its promise to change sections of the PLO charter calling for the destruction of the Jewish state, avoid political activity in Jerusalem and fight Palestinian guerrilla groups opposed to peace deals.
PLO official Hisham Abdel Razek said that after the release one Palestinian female would remain behind bars in Israel -- a 15-year-old arrested two weeks ago trying to stab an Israeli soldier.
He said 28 of the women were convicted of security offences and three were jailed for criminal activity unrelated to the Israeli-Arab conflict.
The release of female, sick and young prisoners was a commitment made in a deal signed by the previous government in September 1995 with the PLO.
Israel released some of the male sick and elderly prisoners but about 5,000 Palestinians are still in its prisons, Palestinian sources said.
